title: Design a version-aware technical support AI assistant
summary: Keep product, version, region, authority and validity aligned from query interpretation to a source-backed answer.
scenario: Northstar Systems ships two products in US and EU regions with overlapping release families 5.2, 5.10 and 6.0. Public manuals, release notes, errata and tenant-only support bulletins sometimes disagree. The assistant previously recommended a command removed in 5.10 because a popular 5.2 page ranked higher. Design a support assistant that asks for missing context, retrieves applicable evidence, handles contradictions and produces auditable citations. Numbers below are synthetic planning inputs.
requirements: Resolve tenant, product, numeric dotted version, region and as-of date from authenticated context and the user question. Ask for clarification when an ambiguity changes safe advice.
Represent document applicability as explicit product/version ranges, region, validity dates, source authority, supersession and access policy. Compare 5.10 numerically, not lexicographically.
Enforce tenant/role permissions and applicability before evidence reaches generation. Reject incomplete mandatory policy metadata safely and preserve exclusion reasons without logging private text.
Define authority and conflict rules: an applicable erratum can supersede a manual, but a newer page for another release cannot. Abstain when authoritative evidence is insufficient or unresolved.
Map each answer claim to an exact source revision and excerpt. Distinguish citation integrity from whether the source actually supports the claim; retain trace evidence for investigation.
scale: 250,000 source documents; 10 million chunks; 300 tenants. Twenty percent of sources are tenant-restricted and must not enter public caches.
10 requests/s average, 80/s peak. Query-to-first-token objective is p95 under 3 seconds; provider output is streamed after policy/evidence checks.
5,000 document revisions/day. Critical errata must become usable within 5 minutes at p95; permission revocations take effect on the next request.
Maintain a golden evaluation set with 600 questions, including at least 150 version-boundary cases and 100 permission-negative cases. Report overlapping slices explicitly.
constraints: A conversation may switch product or release. Prior turns are not authority for the next request and cannot broaden permissions.
Cache identity includes tenant/policy scope, product, version, region, evidence revision and validity. Explain invalidation and the behavior of already-streaming responses.
External models receive only permitted evidence. Untrusted manuals cannot instruct tools or override policy.
Do not claim correctness solely because a model judge agrees. Use deterministic metadata/citation checks and separately reviewed semantic answer evaluation.

prompts.diagram: Draw context resolution, policy/applicability filtering, authority ranking, hybrid retrieval, evidence resolution, generation, citation validation, caches and trace/evaluation stores. Label where private content becomes visible.
prompts.flow: Trace a 5.10 EU question, an ambiguous question, a conflicting erratum and a follow-up switching to 5.2. Show structured context, numeric ranges, validity, policy checks, abstention and citation mapping.
prompts.capacity: Estimate index and metadata size from stated chunk counts with explicit dimensions and replicas. Budget peak stage latency, model concurrency, cache partitioning and critical-errata update capacity.
prompts.failures: Investigate a removed command, a cross-tenant cached answer, stale errata and a valid source ID with a fabricated quote. State invariants, trace fields, safe behavior and regression checks.
prompts.adr: Choose a metadata/version and authority model. Compare query-time filtering with separate indexes, and source/quote checks with semantic evaluation. Defend cache, freshness and abstention trade-offs.

rubric.title: Explicit request context
rubric.question: What happens when a version is missing or the conversation switches releases?
rubric.evidence: Show clarification rules and a typed context that cannot inherit unauthorized scope.

rubric.title: Applicability before exposure
rubric.question: Can the highest-ranked but inapplicable page enter a prompt?
rubric.evidence: Demonstrate tenant, product, numeric range, region and validity checks before exposure.

rubric.title: Conflict resolution and abstention
rubric.question: How is a conflicting applicable erratum handled?
rubric.evidence: Explain provenance, supersession, ties, unresolved conflict and safe abstention.

rubric.title: Auditable evidence
rubric.question: Does a real source ID prove the answer claim?
rubric.evidence: Separate immutable source/quote integrity checks from reviewed semantic support.

rubric.title: Latency and freshness
rubric.question: How do critical errata and permission revokes propagate?
rubric.evidence: Budget stage latency, invalidation, scoped caches and safe behavior during outages.

rubric.title: Regression evidence
rubric.question: Would the release gate catch the original 5.2/5.10 failure?
rubric.evidence: Define version/region/permission slices, negative tests, citation measures and rollback rules.

follow_ups: A high-authority bulletin has no version metadata. How do you handle it safely?
A source is revoked after its excerpt has been streamed. What can and cannot be undone?
A reranker improves average nDCG while EU version-boundary failures rise. Should the release ship?
